input.summary: The packet contains no complete pilot design. The owner asks whether failing to reject a difference establishes equivalence between two algorithms — it does not. A non-significant result or distribution overlap cannot establish equivalence or no effect under the server's descriptive-only policy. Additionally, no practical equivalence margin has been selected, no algorithm identities or input hashes are provided, and no resource bounds are specified. Three clarifying questions are raised before a draft can be compiled.
clarification_questions: What is the practically motivated equivalence margin for TCP flow completion time (e.g., ±X ms or ±Y%) that you would accept as 'no meaningful difference', and how was that threshold chosen from domain requirements rather than from the data?

What are the exact identities (names, versions, and configuration parameters) of the two algorithms you wish to compare, and can you provide SHA-256 hashes or archived snapshots of the input traffic traces or topology configurations to be used?

What are your resource bounds for this pilot — specifically the maximum wall-clock seconds, number of replications, and maximum output bytes — and will you run under the emulated-netem-v1 runner or a different execution environment?

proposal.problem: The packet is empty and the owner's stated goal — showing equivalence by failing to reject a difference — is not supported by a descriptive pilot or by a non-significant result alone.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms delay change TCP flow completion time, and if so by how much, across two named algorithm configurations?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions are implied: (1) baseline — no added delay; (2) treatment — 20 ms added one-way delay. Algorithm identities and all other configuration parameters remain unspecified in the current packet.
proposal.related_work: The source citation is synthetic and unreviewed (sha256: aaaa…aaaa); no full text or prior measurements are available to anchor expected effect sizes or margins.
proposal.alternatives: An independent check against archived emulation data or a new empirical measurement are both possible paths; neither can establish equivalence without a pre-specified, domain-justified margin and a separately reviewed inferential design.
proposal.design: A descriptive pilot would record observed TCP flow completion times under each condition across replicated runs, reporting ranges, medians and configuration contrasts without hypothesis testing or equivalence inference.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: TCP flow completion time (units: milliseconds). Secondary metric: per-flow byte count (units: bytes), to confirm flows completed as intended.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline, packet loss rate, flow size, and number of concurrent flows must be held fixed across conditions; only the added delay varies.
proposal.inputs: Input traffic traces, topology files, and algorithm configurations are not yet identified; SHA-256 hashes and version identifiers are required before a protocol can be locked.
proposal.limitations: Equivalence cannot be concluded from a descriptive pilot or from a non-significant result; a justified margin, estimand specification, and separately reviewed inferential design are prerequisites. Simulation results do not generalize to real-world network performance.
